One of history's darkest chapters unfolded in Nanking, 1937—when the Japanese army unleashed systematic brutality on Chinese civilians. Between 100,000 and 300,000 were slaughtered in just two months. But the horror didn't end there. Unit 731, Japan's secret biological warfare research facility, conducted unspeakable experiments on living prisoners—infecting them with diseases, removing organs while they suffered, and testing weapons on defenseless captives. These atrocities shaped military history and revealed the dangers of unchecked ideology. #simplehistory
